extracted.intended_audience: Lean 3 users porting code to Lean 4 (mathlib4 contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical survival-guide style rules and recommendations for translating Lean 3 code and practices to Lean 4, including syntax, tactic changes, naming conventions, gotchas, and tooling tips for contributors to mathlib4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function notation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Function/lambda notation has changed from `λ x, f x` to `fun x => f x` (or `λ x => f x`, or `fun x ↦ f x`, or `λ x ↦ f x`).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the new `fun`/`=>` (or `↦`) forms when writing lambdas. The page lists multiple equivalent notations to prefer in Lean 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Π/Σ type notation updated
rubrics_metrics.description: Old `Π x : A, P x` and `Σ x : A, P x` notations now have new forms `(x : A) → P x` and `(x : A) × P x`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The old notation still works, but prefer the new arrow/product forms in Lean 4 code for consistency with the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure expansion/`with`-syntax for updates
rubrics_metrics.description: To build a structure that expands other structures, the new syntax is `{ parent1, parent2 with field1 := value1 field2 := value2 }`. If there are no extra fields, use `{ parent1, parent2 with }`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you need to pass a term of a pre-structure type, you can write `my_term : Struct A where preStruct_2.mk := proof1 ... __ : preStruct_1 := proof3`. The final line uses two underscores `__` to indicate passing a term; if the type can be inferred you may omit an explicit type annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern matching uses `=>` and no `end`
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern-match clauses use `=>` instead of `:=`, and `↦` cannot be used in `match` patterns; `match` does not require/end with `end`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: `def Option.str1 : Option Nat → String | some a => "some" ++ toString a | none => "none"`. Be careful to use `=>` and the new indentation/whitespace rules (no `end`).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infix notation uses `·` implicit lambda
rubrics_metrics.description: For infix notation like `+` you can no longer write `(+)` or `(+ n)`; instead use `(· + ·)` or `(· + n)`. The dot `·` (entered with `\.`) is an implicit lambda expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The `·` placeholder is an implicit anonymous argument; it will be inserted at the nearest enclosing parentheses. Use `\.` (not `\cdot`) to type it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application operator `f $ x` replaced by `f <| x` (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new notation `f <| x` exists for the low-precedence application formerly written `f $ x` (the old notation still works).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may adopt `f <| x` for consistency with Lean 4, but legacy `f $ x` remains supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace sensitivity / indentation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Lean 4 is whitespace-sensitive; multi-line commands (`by`, `do`, `match`, tactic block `·`, etc.) are ended by unindenting the first line following the block. Incorrect indentation can make lines out of scope and produce errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows a tactic block where a line indented less than the line above is out of the `·` scope. Pay attention to indentation for tactic blocks, `calc` blocks, matches, and multi-line constructs; small changes in spaces can change scoping.

rubrics_metrics.name: `calc` block syntax is whitespace-sensitive
rubrics_metrics.description: The `calc` block is written like `calc A = B := proof1 _ = C := proof2` and its layout is whitespace-sensitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct indentation within `calc` sequences; spacing affects how the proofs are associated with the steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining terms that expand other structures: use `where` + `__` trick
rubrics_metrics.description: To define a term of a structure that expands other structures, use `my_term : Struct A where ... __ : preStruct_1 := proof3` where the `__` line passes a term of the pre-structure type. If the pre-structure type can be inferred from the RHS, you can omit the explicit type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the older `{Struct := _, ..preStruct_1}` Lean 3 pattern; the VSCode skeleton can still propose many fields from unfolded parent structures, so `__` may be more convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactic mode entry and layout: use `by` + newline + indentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter tactic mode by writing `by` then a newline and indenting following tactic lines (e.g., `by\ntrivial`). Don't put commas after tactics; write the next tactic on a new line in the same column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid trailing commas after tactics; use new line indentation. Example: `example : True := by trivial` or `by` then indented tactics. Tactic blocks must respect column alignment and indentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use `·` for focusing the first goal inside tactic blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: With multiple goals, `· <tactics>` addresses the first goal instead of `{ <tactics> }`. The bullet `·` is typed with `\.` (not `\cdot`).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Lean 4 replacement for the old `{ ... }` goal-focus braces. Keep consistent column alignment when using `·` blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing tactics on one line: `;` and `<;>`
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want multiple tactics on the same line, use `tac1; tac2` (corresponds to Lean 3 `tac1, tac2`) or `tac1 <;> tac2` (corresponds to Lean 3 `tac1; tac2`).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick the appropriate separator to match the old Lean 3 sequencing semantics when porting tactic scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: `_` vs `?_` underscore semantics in tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: `_` should be used for implicit arguments that the elaborator can fill; `?_` produces a new metavariable/subgoal. You can name these produced subgoals `?myName`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use `_` to avoid creating extra goals and `?_` when you want an explicit hole/new goal you can later fill; name holes with `?name` to refer to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactic renames and syntax differences (refine', cases', induction', rw brackets, constructor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several tactic names changed: `refine` → `refine'`, `cases` → `cases'`, `induction` → `induction'`. The square brackets in `rw [h]` are mandatory. `split` has been removed; use `constructor` instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When porting tactics, replace deprecated names with the primed variants and update call syntax (e.g., `rw` must have square-bracketed lemma lists). Replace `split` with `constructor` in proofs that used `split`.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute and locale syntax changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes like `@[simp, priority 100]` are replaced by `@[simp 100]` (you can also use `@[simp low]` or `@[simp high]`). `open_locale foo` is roughly replaced by `open scoped Foo`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update attribute annotations and locale opening forms to Lean 4 equivalents; prefer `open scoped` for localized notation/locale opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions (from porting wiki): terms of `Prop` (proofs, theorem names) use `snake_case`; `Prop`/`Type` objects (inductive types, structures, classes) use `UpperCamelCase`; functions are named like their return values (e.g., a function of type `A → B → C` is named as though it is a term of type `C`); other `Type` terms use `lowerCamelCase`. When an `UpperCamelCase` item is part of something named in `snake_case`, refer to it in `lowerCamelCase`. Acronyms depend on first-character case. Rules apply to fields and constructors; rare exceptions exist and should be discussed on Zulip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these conventions for consistency in mathlib4; be mindful of special-case exceptions and discuss them publicly. The list is taken from the porting wiki and may have edge-case updates there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitfall: stray names in types become fresh variables
rubrics_metrics.description: If you write a name in the type of a declaration that isn't a known declaration or variable, Lean interprets it as a fresh variable (and adds it as an argument to the declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: `example : a + 3 = 3 + a := by rw [Nat.add_comm]` — `a` in the type becomes a variable. Such names are colored differently in the editor; if problematic, disable the behavior with `set_option autoImplicit false`.

rubrics_metrics.name: All variables included in declaration context; `include`/`omit` removed
rubrics_metrics.description: In Lean 4 all variables are included in the context for a declaration (including named instances). `include` and `omit` commands are removed. After elaboration, Lean removes unused variables from the argument list, but during proof-writing all variables appear in the local context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: goal states may look cluttered with variables that are not actual arguments; `induction` generalizes all variables in the local context causing them to appear in the proof term. Workaround: `clear` variables you don't want before using `induction`.

rubrics_metrics.name: New features: named implicit args, `f ..`, and `#align`
rubrics_metrics.description: Named implicit arguments supported: `f (x := 3) a`. You can write `f ..` for multiple unnamed arguments. `#align` connects Lean 3 names to Lean 4 names for mathport and will be removed from mathlib after porting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named implicit arguments to improve clarity and replace verbose `@`-style explicit argument passing. `#align` is a temporary aid for porting mathlib3 names to Lean 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor/navigation features
rubrics_metrics.description: Hovering shows pop-ups with information and you can jump to definitions/notations (F12). When right-clicking a declaration you can go to both 'go to definition' and 'go to declaration'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use editor features to inspect declarations and notations while porting; these improve discoverability during migration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaprogramming changed in Lean 4
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaprogramming works completely differently in Lean 4 compared to Lean 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Lean 4 Metaprogramming book, Functional Programming in Lean, and meta4dummies for guidance; porting metaprograms requires reworking code with Lean 4's metaprogramming APIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cache/tooling: `lake exe cache get` replaces `leanproject get-cache`
rubrics_metrics.description: The previous `leanproject get-cache` command is replaced by `lake exe cache get`, which downloads as many ready-made `.olean` files as possible to speed local builds. Use `lake exe cache get!` (with `!`) to force re-downloading the entire cache if something seems wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run `lake exe cache get` to speed up builds; if downloads or builds behave oddly, run the forced variant with `!` to refresh the cache.
